answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities with a kernel check: each identity keeps a unique kernel of its own recent records, and verifiers sample random entries and ask it to reproduce their computation. A hollow identity holding pointers to another identity's kernel fails, since reproduction needs the original data. The records are split across karst stores, so a compromised store exposes only a fraction of one kernel. One honest agent maintains one kernel; an attacker with 1,000 fakes must store 1,000 distinct kernels, and a copied kernel is caught by sampling and stripped of standing.
